title: Local Parity and Systematic Peterson Counterexamples in the Motivic Hit Problem
summary: The motivic hit problem asks for a minimal set of module generators of $H^{*,*}(BV_n;\mathbb F_2)$ over the mod~$2$ motivic Steenrod algebra. Kameko proved that the motivic Peterson-type analogue of Wood's theorem fails by constructing monomials $z_k$ which are not hit even when the corresponding topological degree may satisfy $β(d)>n$. His proof passes to $N_n=M_n/(τ)$ and analyzes, in degree $d=k+2d_1$ with $d_1=(n-1)(2^k-1)$, a distinguished summand whose basis consists of the monotone translates of $z_k$.
